paragraphs.text: Alias Chelubai, or Caleb. {1Ch 2:9; 1Ch 2:18}
Who was the posthumous son of Hezron. {1Ch 2:24}
Who this Coz was, we read not anywhere: Videntur lacunae quaedam esse in hoc capite. Some think he was one of the sons of Ashur by his wife Helah: though he be not reckoned with the rest. {1Ch 4:7}

Propter opes, saith Piscator, for his wealth; for his holiness rather, {see Isa 43:4} or for his valour and learning, tam Marte quam Mercurio, if he were that renowned Othniel, {Jdg 1:13} as some make him to be: others, Othniel’s brother. {1Ch 4:13} In his city, called by his name Jabez, dwelt scribes, {1Ch 2:55} hence Vatablus concludeth that he was doctor insignis. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And Jabez was more honourable than his brethren.

paragraphs.text: {b} i.e., Dolorificum; a dear, but doleful child to her, a son of her sorrows, because she had a hard bargain, as they call it, when she brought him forth; and haply died of him, as Rachel did of her Benoni. His father might change his name to Othniel.
paragraphs.anchor: And his mother called him Jabez

paragraphs.text: {a} Clarissimus fuit propter foritudinem; deinde doctor fuit. - Lavat.
{b} Jangbets, for Jangtseb; of gnetseb, pain, grief.
Upon the point of some warlike exploit: or in some great exigency. And hence he was "more honourable"; {1Ch 4:9} he prayed earnestly, and sped accordingly.
paragraphs.anchor: And Jabez called on the God of Israel.

paragraphs.text: Heb., If blessing thou wilt bless me: q.d., then shalt thou have mine utmost service, and I will wholly devote myself to thy fear. This was to "pray in the Holy Ghost"; this was to do, as afterwards Christ did, who "being in an agony prayed more earnestly." {Luk 22:44}
paragraphs.anchor: Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed.

paragraphs.text: Pray we with like fervency, And enlarge my heart.
He labours in prayer lustily, and followeth his suit close.
paragraphs.anchor: And that thine hand might be with me.

paragraphs.text: “ Una est in trepida mihi re medicina, Iehovae
Cot patrium, os verax, omnipotensque manus. ”

And that thou wouldest keep me from evil.] Or, Cause that evil grieve me not. He seemeth in this request to allude to his own name, q.d., I have my name from sorrow; but I would not be crushed with sorrow. This might be his prayer to God, even while he was fighting against his enemies.
Called Hushah. {1Ch 4:4}
This, Lyra taketh to be the name of a place: others render it teneros vel nobiles, these were gentlemen or nobles.
paragraphs.anchor: These are the men of Rechah.

paragraphs.text: See on 1Ch 4:9-10.

Opifices Deo curae sunt. God takes notice of, and care for poor handicraftsmen, who live by their hard labour, who get it and eat it. Yea, the apostle Peter showeth that a poor servant, when he suffereth hard words and ill usage from his master, doth herein find acceptance with God. {1Pe 2:19-20}
And grandson of Kenez: whence Caleb is called the Kenezite, {Num 32:12} saith Diodate.
Not that learned scribe, {Ezr 7:1} - there is a difference in the last letter of their names - but the son, as it seems, of Asareel.
i.e., Bithiah {1Ch 4:18} bare.
The name of a man in this place.
Gentis opificii byssini, silk-weavers. See on 1Ch 4:14.
paragraphs.anchor: Of them that wrought fine linen.

paragraphs.text: Ruled as viceroys under the kings of Judah, who had subdued Moab.
paragraphs.anchor: Who had the dominion in Moab.

paragraphs.text: Old and obsolete, Vatablus rendereth it. Ista nomina sunt virorum veterum, these are the names of such as lived long since. Haec sunt nomina prisca priscorum heroum: A Lapide. Thus writeth Ezra; who yet lived before that Socrates taught in Athens, and before any chronicles of the world now extant in the world. Such is the antiquity of holy writ.

Hedge rogues, Mr Dyke {a} calleth them: the base brood of their degenerated forefathers, saith another; poor-spirited men; not like that late learned martyr, who in his banishment or flight for conscience, served the mason; nor like Musculus, forced to dig in the town ditch one while for a poor livelihood; but such as choose rather to abide under the hedges of Babylon, and there to plant gardens, make fences and flower pots for the king of Babylon, than to return to their own country, though Cyrus had proclaimed liberty for them so to do.
paragraphs.anchor: Those that dwelt among plants and hedges.

paragraphs.text: Or, Remained, namely, in Babylon, in the service of the king of that place, being miserable by their own election. These are res obsoletae, things worn out and forgotten; and indeed they deserve to be forgotten. For such the Church prayeth, {Psa 126:4} "Turn again our captivity, O Lord, as the streams in the south." Piscator gathereth from this text, that Ezra wrote this book after the return from Babylon.
{a} Serm. on John v.

His genealogy is set down next to that of Judah, because his lot fell out to be in the tribe of Judah, for most part, {Jos 19:1} though his posterity took part with the other nine tribes in the revolt from Judah and Benjamin, who clave still to the house of David. Of this tribe was that shameless fornicator, Zimri, {Num 25:14} as also Judas Iscariot, as Jerome affirmeth.
None mentioned in these genealogies had so many.
i.e., In vico vulpis, Vat.
Who restored Ziklag and some others of them to the tribe of Judah, saith Lyra.

Called before villages, because unwalled, haply. The Hague in Holland hath two thousand households in it: the inhabitants will not wall it, they say, as desiring to have it counted rather the principal village of Europe, than a lesser city.

This tempted the Simeonites to set upon them, as the wealth of Cyprus did the old Romans; {a} and as the pearls usually cast out with the flood and gathered at the ebb, drew Caesar’s affection for the conquest of Britain. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: And they found fat pasture and good.

paragraphs.text: See on Jdg 18:27-28.
The cursed Canaanites.
paragraphs.anchor: And they of Ham had dwelt there.

paragraphs.text: {a} Sext. Rufus
{b} {Suetonius, Julius Caesar, l. 1. c. 47. 1:95}

In the beginning of his reign; for in the sixth year of his reign the ten tribes were carried captive by Shalmaneser. {2Ki 18:10-11} So that it seems these Simeonites did not long enjoy their new conquests God often punisheth the wicked by others as wicked.
paragraphs.anchor: Came in the days of Hezekiah.

paragraphs.text: As Simeon himself was a rough-spirited venturous man; so were his posterity.
paragraphs.anchor: And some of them, even of the sons of Simeon.

paragraphs.text: Whose preservation from the sword of Joshua, {Exo 17:13} of Saul, {1Sa 15:7} and of David, {2Sa 8:12} was but a reservation to this utter destruction, which God had solemnly sworn, with hand laid upon his own throne. {Exo 17:16}
paragraphs.anchor: And they smote the rest of the Amalekites.
